thread:
anya: Hey team, ran a long-replay sanity pass on the new int4 candidate and hit a weird divergence after ~18k tokens. Not a full failure but model output drifts compared to fp16 baseline.

martin: Ugh. Which testset and quant settings?

anya: testset = long_convo_goldset_v2, quant = int4-legacy (per-shard packing), RoPE scale was set to 'auto' in the compile. Command:
```
./scripts/eval_longctx.sh --model orpheus-32k-int4 --quant int4-legacy --ctx 32768 --seed 1234 --replay true
```
Output shows a subtle token shift starting at token 17992.

jess: Do you see it in logits or just top-1 text?

anya: Both. The token probability distribution moves a bit; top-5 still overlaps heavily but beam scoring prefers different continuation. Snip of log lines:
```
[17990] token="the" p=0.028
[17991] token="meeting" p=0.015
[17992] token="." p=0.009 vs fp16 p=0.021
```

martin: Could be RoPE scaling + kernel selection mismatch under int4. Did the compile pick legacy rotary kernels?

anya: Yes, runtime selected rot_kern_v1 due to short-seq heuristics but sequence length is long. My hypothesis: wrapping/interpolation error at extreme indices.

jess: Can you repro with force-rot_kern_v2? Also try anchored-prefill (no streaming) vs in-flight KV.

anya: Good idea — forced kernel and two modes planned. Running now.

ci-bot: Build 2024.11.2 finished on shard-gpu-12 for orpheus-32k-int4.

martin: Also test with RoPE clamp enabled/disabled. We saw earlier that clamp=true reduced drift in some quantized runs.

anya: Quick note: when I disabled KV caching entirely the divergence disappeared (slow but matches fp16). So it smells like cache index mapping or priming offset problem rather than quantization alone.

jess: That strongly points at the handoff between prefill and in-flight KV offset arithmetic. Any chance of off-by-one when compaction happens?

anya: I'm dumping KV index fingerprints now:
```
# kv_fingerprint dump (first 6 entries)
0: 0x9a3b...
1: 0x4f2c...
17990: 0x1d7a...
17991: 0x1d7b...
17992: 0x1d7c...
```
They look contiguous, but when streaming enabled there is a repeated index at 17992 in one shard.

martin: Repeated index — that would explain probability skew. Is the shard join logic deduping correctly? Did we recently change the broker's ringbuffer shrink?

anya: We merged the broker shrink patch last week (PR #4123). It changes prefill compaction heuristics. Could be interaction.

jess: Plan: (1) force rot_kern_v2 + clamp=true with KV streaming, (2) same with KV disabled, (3) run with old broker binary (pre-PR4123) to compare. Collect logits + kv_fingerprints. I'll help run comparisons.

anya: Running (1) now. ETA ~8h for full goldset. Posting quick sample after 30m.

martin: If we can get a minimal repro that hits the repeated index quickly (maybe by crafting a prefix that triggers compaction thresholds) we can bisect faster. Try a synthetic prompt that pads to boundary around 18k.

anya: Good call. I made a short synthetic that pads to 17990 with repeated anchors and got the repeat in ~6s. Pushing the script:
```
python experiments/quick_repro.py --model orpheus-32k-int4 --pad 17990 --streaming on
```
Output: repeated kv index observed at offset 2 after compaction.

jess: Nice. Can you save the run dir and tag it repro/replica-17992? Share the link.

anya: saved to s3://redwood-ml/repro/repro-17992.tar.gz (permissions open to eng-ml).

martin: I'll pull and run a local bisect with/without PR4123. Also we'll add a telemetry counter for kv-index-dup during compaction to catch it in e2e.

anya: Added a quick watch in the runtime, logging when duplicate index found: "KV_DUP_DETECTED shard=%d idx=%d prefill=%d". It fired on the synthetic run.

jess: Solid. If dup only occurs with streaming + broker shrink + rot_kern_v1 then it's an interaction bug. Prioritize: revert shrink patch on dedicated or add safe-guard.

ci-bot: Deploy job queued: revert/shrink-guard on canary pool.

anya: I'll continue the forced kernel runs and post logs. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

martin: Thanks Anya — ping here when you have the kernel comparison. We'll pair on the revert if needed.
